## Source: amazon-inspector (c686d2223600d1e566907147f1f905b5ecd66809e16c8541262283e425b8bfae)
The package advertises an Instagram scraper but its exported functions are empty stubs. The tarball and wheel ship an 8.4 MB Windows PE (Go-compiled) as src/instantscrape/pip.webp, declared as package_data. The top-level main.py unconditionally calls init() on import; on Windows (os.name=='nt') this moves the bundled pip.webp to the user's home directory as pip.exe (filename reconstructed from the reversed literal "exe.pip"[::-1]) and launches it via ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW with the "runas" verb, triggering a UAC elevation prompt. A sentinel file name is likewise hidden as a reversed literal ("ses.retsboLneddiH"[::-1] -> HiddenLobsters.ses), and the payload uses a.webp extension to masquerade as an image. setup.py additionally registers a custom install cmdclass that invokes `python src/instantscrape/init_scarper.py` after install, routing the sdist install path to the same dropper module. The combination of an opaque bundled Windows executable, reversed-string filename obfuscation, extension masquerade, an empty advertised API, and automatic elevated execution on import is a trojan dropper, not a scraper library.
